title: Live Invocation Harmonizer — streaming rename-resolution and audit-safe payload transformer
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Customers have mixed workloads that still emit legacy 'function' calls while newer clients and third-party integrations use OpenAI-style 'tools'. Our current approach (static alias registry + ad-hoc shims) fails for streaming invocations, breaks provenance, and has caused at least two customer regressions during rollouts. Goal: Implement a streaming-first, low-latency invocation harmonizer that resolves names and payload shapes at runtime, preserves invocation provenance for audit/rollback, and can fall back safely to legacy handlers without requiring client changes.
background: Many existing tickets cover mapping and compatibility (alias registries, name collisions, backfills), but none address the intersection of streaming (token-by-token responses), partial/incremental payloads (streamed tool args), and audit requirements. This ticket builds a runtime component that sits in the request path and performs: 1) deterministic name resolution with conflict rules, 2) payload shape translation (legacy->tool or tool->legacy), 3) provenance tagging so callers can see transformation history, and 4) streaming-safe behavior (no buffering that violates latency SLOs).
acceptance_criteria: New harmonizer protobuf + runtime module implemented and reachable behind a feature flag
Streaming test harness shows end-to-end invocation with 95th percentile added latency < 5ms for name resolution on p99 path
Telemetry emitted: original_name, resolved_name, resolution_strategy, transformation_applied, provenance_id
Transformation preserves required fields and includes a stable provenance header in responses and telemetry
Automated integration tests demonstrate safe fallback to legacy function handler when mapped tool is not available
Documentation (console + API changelog) and migration guide published to Confluence/Docs
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM usage for provenance signing approved
design_decisions: Use deterministic resolution order: explicit alias table > name-normalization heuristic > fuzzy-match heuristic (with threshold)
Provenance model: append-only 'transformations' array with short stable provenance_id (UUIDv4) and signer metadata
Do not buffer streaming tool arguments end-to-end; perform translations on completed argument chunks and allow early streaming of tool outputs when safe
Expose resolution metadata to callers via the existing invocations.trace header to avoid API breakage
Feature-flag the component per-customer and per-route for gradual rollout
tradeoffs: Heavier metadata in requests/responses increases token overhead but gives observability for rollbacks
Deterministic heuristics reduce surprises but may miss legitimate renames — we add a feedback loop to register new aliases
Avoiding buffering keeps latency low, but edge-cases exist when streamed args are split across partial events — we add reassembly heuristics with strict size/timeouts
Signing provenance with HMAC adds CPU but provides tamper evidence; we’ll benchmark and gate with flag
technical_notes: Implementation split: (1) name-resolver service (low-latency in-memory store replicated per-region), (2) transform worker library used by serving runtime, (3) streaming-aware reassembler in runtime that only reassembles when chunk boundaries indicate incomplete JSON/structured payloads. Use existing alias registry tables as initial source of truth and add a small scheduled backfill job to surface unmapped legacy names for operator review.
telemetry_plan: Emit invocation.harmonizer.resolve (tags: customer_id, route, original_name, resolved_name, strategy, duration_ms)
Emit invocation.harmonizer.transform (tags: provenance_id, fields_removed, fields_added, size_delta_bytes)
Add dashboard in Console: harmonizer resolution rate, failure rate, avg latency, list of top unmapped legacy names
Hook alerts: >1% failed resolution over 5m per-customer triggers pager
rollout_plan: Stage 1: unit/integration tests + internal dogfood on staging (feature flag on for internal org)
Stage 2: enable per-route feature flag for low-traffic customers and observe metrics for 48h
Stage 3: expand to customers with streaming workloads, enable HMAC signing in observability only
Stage 4: full enablement with optional automatic alias registration after operator approval
test_plan: Create streaming integration tests that simulate partial arg delivery and verify transform correctness
Fuzz test name heuristics with randomized ascii/unicode names and collision scenarios
Performance benchmark per-region to ensure < 5ms p95 resolution latency under 10k rps
End-to-end regression tests to ensure no change to existing legacy function semantics unless mapping applies
implementation_tasks: ENG: build name-resolver service with in-memory replica and watch support
ENG: add transform library to runtime (C++/Rust worker and Java/Node bindings as needed)
ENG: streaming reassembler with chunk-safe JSON heuristics
ENG: telemetry instrumentation and Console dashboard integration
ENG: feature-flag control and rollout scripts
DOCS: migration guide and changelog entry
risks: Misresolution causing silent semantic changes to tool calls — mitigated by conservative default (no-op unless high-confidence match)
Increased CPU for HMAC signing under high throughput — mitigated by sampling and optional signing per-customer
Edge-case JSON reassembly causing additional latency for pathological chunking — mitigate via reassembly timeout and fallback to buffering with operator alert
